sentences.text: Crymocetus translates to 'cold sea monster' and represents an extinct reptile from the Late Cretaceous Chalk Group of Sussex, England.
Scientists know this animal only through a single posterior cervical vertebra discovered in the Chalk Group of Sussex, England.
Sir Richard Owen first described the specimen as Plesiosaurus bernardi in 1850.
Edward Drinker Cope later established the genus Crymocetus in 1869 after re-examining the holotype of Plesiosaurus bernardi.
Cope originally placed Crymocetus in Elasmosauridae, though later researchers suggested it belonged to Pliosauridae or Rhomaleosauridae.
Today, Crymocetus is classified within Plesiosauria incertae sedis due to uncertain placement.
Many paleontologists ignored Cope's name Crymocetus, and Lydekker synonymized it with Cimoliasaurus in 1889.
Researchers suggest that Crymocetus requires a restudy alongside other Cretaceous plesiosaurs from England.
